name: Curve-steepening regime ARMS long-XLF (bank net-interest-margin sleeve, SPY-disconfirmed)
rationale: Thesis: a steepening 2s10s curve mechanically widens bank net-interest margins, so financials (XLF) carry a regime-conditional drift that plain sector momentum misses. The orthogonal structure is regime-GATING: only take the XLF trend when the curve is STEEPENING (yield_curve_2s10s crossing UP through a fitted trailing reference — the DIRECTION, never the slow raw level) AND the macro regime is turning early-cycle/risk-on (macro_regime cross_up), with XLF's own short-window return positive as the trend confirm. Documented (ainvest 'Great Rotation', Curzio Research, Capital Group): financials outperform the S&P by 5-10% in steepening regimes when loan demand recovers and credit losses peak. Macro desks trade this via rate futures + XLF options with leverage; a long-only daily XLF sleeve gated on the curve is a low-capacity scrap they leave on the table. DISCONFIRMERS: (1) XLF-trend-alone (same ret_Nd>0, no curve/regime gate): if indistinguishable, the curve adds nothing and it is just sector momentum. (2) SPY control: run the identical curve+regime gate on SPY instead of XLF — if SPY captures the same lift, the gate is merely timing broad-market risk-on, NOT the financials-specific NIM channel, and the XLF specificity is illusory. The XLF-gated version must beat both nets of fees. (3) Level-trap control: using cross_up on the curve (not a gt on the raw bounded level) is what separates true steepening alpha from a near-constant always-true level threshold. NOTE: macro_regime is FRED-T10Y2Y-derived, so the regime arm and the curve arm share a root series; it is included as a distinct transform/regime tag, and the SPY disconfirmer is the real test that the lift is XLF-specific NIM and not just curve-timed beta.
catalyst: 2s10s steepening turns positive / accelerates as the Fed cycle shifts to easing and loan demand recovers — financials re-rate on widening net-interest margins.
